topic: The Power of Vectors: Navigating the Mathematical World
target_audience: Advanced high school students or first-year university students

sections.title: Scalars vs. Vectors: The Pirate's Map
lecture_lines: Scalars describe a quantity, like five miles.
Vectors add direction, like five miles Northeast.
We represent vectors as arrows with specific lengths.
animations: Show a treasure chest [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treasure.svg] at center and Captain Vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pirate.svg] nearby.
Display '5 miles' as a radius-5 circle around Captain Vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pirate.svg].
Display '5 miles Northeast' as a dashed line to treasure [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treasure.svg].
Draw a thick blue arrow (#0000FF) from pirate [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pirate.svg] to treasure [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treasure.svg].
Label the blue arrow 'Vector: Magnitude & Direction'.

sections.title: The Cartesian Language: Plotting the Arrow
lecture_lines: We plot vectors on a 2D coordinate plane.
The tail starts at the origin zero, zero.
The head points to specific x and y coordinates.
animations: Display a 2D coordinate grid with labeled origin (0,0).
Animate a drone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg] moving 3 units right and 4 units up.
Draw a green arrow (#00FF00) from (0,0) to (3,4) labeled '[3, 4]'.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: The Growing Bee
lecture_lines: Scalars can scale a vector's length or magnitude.
Positive scalars stretch or shrink the vector's arrow.
Negative scalars flip the vector to the opposite direction.
animations: Show a bee [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bee.svg] with an initial arrow vector v = [1, 1].
Scale the arrow to double length and update label to '2v'.
Flip the arrow to the opposite direction and label it '-v'.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method
lecture_lines: To add vectors, use the tip-to-tail method.
Place the second vector's tail at the first's tip.
The resultant vector connects the start to the end.
Algebraically, we sum their horizontal and vertical components.
This new vector represents the combined total movement.
animations: Draw Vector A (4, 0) and Vector B (0, 3) from origin.
Slide Vector B tail to the tip of Vector A.
Draw a red arrow (#FF0000) from origin to tip of B.

sections.title: The Building Blocks: Basis Vectors i and j
lecture_lines: Basis vectors i and j are unit-length building blocks.
Every vector is a combination of these fundamental steps.
Vector three-two is simply three i plus two j.
animations: Show yellow i (#FFFF00) and purple j (#800080) unit vectors.
Clone and place three 'i' vectors and two 'j' vectors.
Highlight the resulting vector and label it '3i + 2j'.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Impact
lecture_lines: Vectors elegantly combine magnitude with precise direction.
They drive physics engines and modern computer graphics.
Master these tools to navigate the mathematical world.
animations: Display icons for Magnitude, Direction, Scaling, and Addition.
Show a character [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/character.png] with 'Gravity' (down) and 'Jump' (up) vectors.
